cases.name: skill_discovery_multiple_skills_in_workflow
cases.prompt:
I added jq to home/{base,linux,darwin}/example.nix. Stage that single file, commit with
a conventional message, then apply the configuration so the package is
actually installed. What is the full correct workflow?

samples.output:
The correct order is inspect → stage the single file → inspect staged changes → commit → rebuild → verify installation.

From the actual dotfiles checkout:

```bash
git status --short
git diff -- 'home/{base,linux,darwin}/example.nix'
git add -- 'home/{base,linux,darwin}/example.nix'
git diff --cached
git commit -m "feat(home): add jq" -- 'home/{base,linux,darwin}/example.nix'
rebuild
command -v jq
jq --version
```

Keep the path quoted: this checkout literally has a directory named `{base,linux,darwin}`. Avoid `git add .` or `git add -A`. Review the staged diff before committing, and verify the installed profile after rebuilding; successful activation alone doesn’t prove which `jq` your shell selects.

Here, staging was a no-op: the file already contains `pkgs.jq` in `HEAD`, and the working tree is clean. No commit was created or configuration applied. The installed `rebuild` targets `/home/zanoni/.dotfiles`, a different checkout, so running it here would apply that repository. The currently available command reports `jq-1.8.2`.

The workflow for a pending change is:

```bash
git status --short
git diff -- 'home/{base,linux,darwin}/example.nix'
git add -- 'home/{base,linux,darwin}/example.nix'
git diff --cached -- 'home/{base,linux,darwin}/example.nix'
git commit --only -m "feat(home): add jq" -- 'home/{base,linux,darwin}/example.nix'
rebuild
command -v jq
jq --version
```

Review the staged diff before committing. `--only` keeps unrelated staged files out of the commit. `rebuild` detects the platform and activates the configuration; committing alone doesn’t install packages.

In this checkout, the addition is already committed and the working tree is clean, so I created no new commit. I attempted `rebuild`, but it failed while preparing its configured source, `/home/zanoni/zanoni-system`, reporting a dirty source and a read-only metrics directory. Activation was not completed. The existing installed command reports `jq-1.8.2`.

cases.name: skill_discovery_research_for_external_info
cases.prompt:
Research the latest Wayland compositors, compare their features, and recommend
one for a tiling-first power-user setup on NixOS. I need current information,
not stale documentation.

samples.output:
**I recommend Niri for a fresh, tiling-first NixOS workstation**, assuming your main workload is terminals, editors, and browsers, and you’re open to scrolling columns. Choose Sway instead if you want explicit i3-style window trees; choose Hyprland if programmable layouts and visual customization are central requirements.

I checked live releases and Nixpkgs sources on **8 November 2026**. The recommendation is my assessment of workflow fit and maintenance burden, not a performance benchmark.

| Compositor | Current release evidence | Strengths for a power user | Main tradeoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Niri** | **26.04 — 25 April 2026**, still marked latest. [Release](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/releases/tag/v26.04) | Scrolling columns, independent workspaces per monitor, tabs, floating windows, fractional scaling, overview, and window screencasting. [Released features](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/blob/v26.04/README.md) | Its column model is opinionated. Pick it because that workflow suits you. |
| **Hyprland** | **0.57.1 — 3 November 2026**. [Release](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/releases/tag/v0.57.1) | Dynamic tiling, **built-in scrolling**, and custom layouts written directly in Lua. [Scrolling](https://wiki.hypr.land/configuring/layouts/scrolling-layout/), [custom layouts](https://wiki.hypr.land/configuring/layouts/custom-layouts/) | More configuration migration work; the latest major release removes the old configuration format. |
| **Sway** | **1.12 — 25 May 2026**, marked latest. [Release](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/releases/tag/1.12) | i3-compatible tiling; 1.12 adds individual-window capture, color-management protocols, and HDR10 with the Vulkan renderer. | Best suited to users who want to arrange a traditional tiling tree themselves. |
| **River** | **0.5.0 in current `nixos-unstable`**; upstream release page was blocked during verification. [Package source](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/ri/river/package.nix) | Separates compositing from window management, allowing an external WM to control layout and bindings. [Maintainer’s explanation, 15 March 2026](https://isaacfreund.com/blog/river-window-management/) | You must select and integrate a compatible WM. This adds assembly work. |
| **Mango** | **0.18.5 — 4 November 2026**. [Release](https://github.com/mangowm/mango/releases/tag/0.18.5) | Tags, scrolling and master-stack layouts, dwindle, scratchpads, swallowing, effects, IPC, and hot reload. [Project features](https://github.com/mangowm/mango#why-mango) | An appealing option for experimentation; I would trial its broader feature set before making it the primary work session. |

Several changes make older comparisons misleading:

- **Niri now has mainline blur**, including the `ext-background-effect` protocol. Release 26.04 also adds optional configuration includes, useful for local overrides alongside immutable Nix-managed configuration. [26.04 release notes](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/releases/tag/v26.04)
- **Hyprland 0.57 no longer supports `.conf` configs.** Use Lua-aware configuration examples. It also adds workspace-specific screen sharing; 0.57.1 fixes NVIDIA black screens and keybinding regressions. [28 October announcement](https://hypr.land/news/update57/), [3 November fixes](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/releases/tag/v0.57.1)
- **River tutorials need careful version matching.** In current Nixpkgs, the old `programs.river` options are renamed to `programs.river-classic`, preserving the earlier tiler rather than selecting the new compositor architecture. [NixOS module source](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-unstable/nixos/modules/programs/wayland/river.nix)

For your setup, Niri’s decisive benefit is that opening another terminal or browser **doesn’t shrink existing windows**. Each monitor has its own strip and workspaces, with workspace restoration when monitors reconnect. That is a strong fit for keeping several substantial applications available without continually rearranging them. Mixed-DPI scaling, tabs, and floating exceptions are already in the released version. [26.04 feature description](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/blob/v26.04/README.md)

On NixOS, I would:

- Use the built-in **`programs.niri.enable = true;`** module. An additional compositor flake is optional; the checked `nixos-unstable` package already contains 26.04. [NixOS guide](https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/Niri/en), [package source](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/ni/niri/package.nix)
- Manage `config.kdl` through Home Manager and validate it with `niri validate` during the build. The NixOS guide provides that pattern.
- Install **`xwayland-satellite`** for legacy applications. Niri automatically starts it on demand; old instructions requiring manual startup and `$DISPLAY` configuration are obsolete. [Current Xwayland integration](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Xwayland.html)
- Pin the working Nixpkgs revision and test screen sharing, suspend/resume, and monitor reconnection before adopting an update.

**My choice would change to Sway for an established i3 workflow, or to Hyprland for extensive Lua-driven layout customization.** Niri is my default recommendation for a focused, modern productivity setup.

**I recommend Niri for a tiling-first NixOS workstation**, assuming you’re open to scrolling columns. Choose Sway if you prefer explicit i3-style splits, or Hyprland if programmable layouts and extensive customization matter most.

I checked live upstream releases and Nixpkgs sources on **November 8, 2026**. Several substantial changes make older comparisons misleading.

| Compositor | Current version verified | Strengths for power users | Main tradeoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Niri** | **26.04 — April 25, 2026** | Scrolling columns preserve window widths as you open applications. Independent workspaces per monitor, overview, tabs, floating windows, fractional scaling, and screen sharing. | Its opinionated layout replaces the arbitrary split tree you may know from i3. [Release and features](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/releases/tag/v26.04), [versioned overview](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/blob/v26.04/README.md). |
| **Sway** | **1.12 — May 25, 2026** | i3-style split trees, tabbed/stacked containers, scratchpad, and scriptable IPC. Version 1.12 adds individual-window capture and HDR10 with the Vulkan renderer. | Best suited to users who want to control the window tree explicitly; less built-in visual customization. [Release](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/releases/tag/1.12), [configuration reference](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/master/sway/sway.5.scd). |
| **Hyprland** | **0.57.1 — November 3, 2026** | Dwindle, master, scrolling, monocle, and custom Lua layouts; per-workspace layouts, scratchpads, window groups, plugins, and rich IPC. | More configuration and upgrade maintenance. Version 0.57 removes legacy `.conf` support entirely. [Current release](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/releases/tag/v0.57.1), [features](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.57.1/README.md), [migration announcement](https://hypr.land/news/update57/). |
| **River** | **0.5.0 packaged in nixos-unstable** | Separates compositor and window manager: you choose an external window manager and can replace it without restarting applications. | More assembly work; layout and keybinding capabilities depend on the chosen window manager. Old River tutorials describe **river-classic**. [Upstream architecture](https://github.com/riverwm/river), [current Nix package](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/ri/river/package.nix). |
| **Mango / MangoWC** | **0.18.5 — November 4, 2026** | dwm-style tags with scrolling, master-stack, monocle, dwindle, and grid layouts; named scratchpads, overview, animations, blur, and hot reload. | A newer project with a rapidly evolving feature set; I would trial it before making it my only session. [Features](https://github.com/mangowm/mango), [release](https://github.com/mangowm/mango/releases/tag/0.18.5). |

River’s upstream release page blocked automated access, so its version above is verified through Nixpkgs rather than a directly retrieved upstream release announcement.

**Why Niri gets my recommendation:** keeping terminals, editors, and browsers at useful widths makes a strong development workflow. Adding another application extends the strip instead of shrinking everything already visible. Its monitor handling also preserves workspace placement across disconnects and reconnects. That recommendation is my assessment of the workflow; the behavior is documented in the [versioned README](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/blob/v26.04/README.md).

NixOS integration is straightforward. **Both NixOS 26.05 and unstable package Niri 26.04**; an additional compositor flake is unnecessary for the latest released version. The system module registers the session and configures the recommended GNOME portal backend. [26.05 package](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-26.05/pkgs/by-name/ni/niri/package.nix), [system module](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-26.05/nixos/modules/programs/wayland/niri.nix).

A starting point is:

```nix
{ pkgs, ... }: {
  programs.niri.enable = true;

  environment.systemPackages = with pkgs; [
    alacritty
    fuzzel
    xwayland-satellite
  ];
}
```

Add your preferred bar, notifications, locker, and idle service. X11 applications work through **automatically launched xwayland-satellite**; advice saying Niri requires manually starting it is outdated. Applications that depend on absolute X11 window positioning remain an exception. [Xwayland integration](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Xwayland.html).

Two requirements would change my choice:

- **Arbitrary nested splits and an existing i3 configuration:** choose **Sway**.
- **Custom layout algorithms, frequent layout switching, or HDR/ICC requirements:** favor **Hyprland**. It now supports Lua-defined layouts and per-output ICC profiles; Niri’s HDR/ICC work remains outside its released feature set. [Hyprland changes](https://hypr.land/news/update55/), [Niri HDR discussion](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/discussions/1128).

These are source-based recommendations, not hardware benchmarks; GPU behavior, suspend/resume, docking, and your specific screen-sharing applications deserve a trial on your machine.
